# v1.9.1 — In-app updates use a stable signing key

- Fixed Android refusing to install CI-built updates over an existing app because each CI run previously generated a different fallback signing key.
- Committed and configured the same release keystore for local and CI APK builds, matching the identity used by prior local releases; corrected the keystore path so the intended key is actually used.
- Added CI checks that the committed keystore loads and that the built APK certificate SHA-256 matches the expected release fingerprint. A mismatched signature now fails the release instead of shipping an un-installable update.
- Replaced the constant Android `versionCode` with a date-based value so updates advance monotonically.
- The mobile updater can install matching signed updates directly over the installed app.

## Important key handling

- Do not lose or regenerate the committed keystore. Before a Play Store release, rotate the signing setup and store the key securely in GitHub Secrets.
- Mobile package version: **1.9.1+7**.
